solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 19 down to 18); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In High Mass a participant inserted insulting language

indicators.note: inserted says one piece is put inside another
high as in drunk or wild, so the letters of these words reel about into a new order

parts.note: RC, a Roman Catholic, is the kind of worshipper taking part in a High Mass

explanation.surface: A worshipper at a solemn service mutters something rude under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like part of 'High Mass' but signals an anagram of MASS A, giving SAASM; 'inserted' puts RC (Roman Catholic) after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is mocking, cutting speech, a form of insult delivered with irony.

clue.text: Diver has drunk gallons

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the word before are reeling about

explanation.surface: A deep-sea diver has downed gallons of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' is the seabird, a cormorant relative, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of cormorant, a seabird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Free, about to go on holiday, it's said

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: leave is time off work, so a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone is freed and about to head off on a break, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a burden is to free them of it.

clue.text: A short bird hauled up deep plants

indicators.note: in a down clue hauled up means read from the bottom upwards
short says the bird's name loses its final letter

parts.note: an eagle is a bird

explanation.surface: A briefly glimpsed bird is pulled up from the sea plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims EAGLE to EAGL; 'hauled up' turns it to LGAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are algae, simple plant-like organisms living in deep water.

clue.text: In Paris, he has quit butchering for a change

indicators.note: has quit says these letters leave the longer word

parts.note: butchering a body is mutilation
il is French for he

explanation.surface: A Parisian man gives up the butcher's trade for something new.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutation is an alteration, especially in genetics.

clue.text: Son replaces hydrogen in car perhaps, causing blister

indicators.note: replaces says one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: a car is an example of a vehicle
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry-flavoured image of swapping fuel in a car, ending in a painful burn.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesicle is a small fluid-filled sac on the skin, which is a blister in medical terms.

clue.text: Marines board vessel to find pests

indicators.note: board as in boarding a ship, so these letters get on inside the word for vessel

parts.note: a vein is a blood vessel
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Marines climb aboard a ship to hunt for rats.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessel is a blood vessel, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats, mice and other nuisance animals are collectively pests.

clue.text: Fatty uses cab travelling around Devon regularly

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the pair picked from the county
travelling says these letters move into another order
regularly picks every other letter of the county name

explanation.surface: An overweight person takes a taxi around a West Country county.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its even letters are E and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum, an oily substance, so the word means fatty or greasy.

clue.text: Make boxes millions burn

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the verb for make holds the abbreviation

parts.note: to make is to create
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A manufacturer packs millions of things to set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate is to burn a body to ashes.

clue.text: Winemaker's big blunder in Times

definitions.note: read as the winemaker is: this fruit makes a home-made wine

parts.note: a big brother is the elder one

indicators.note: in puts the mistake inside the word for times

parts.note: by as in multiplication, three by four
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A huge mistake in the Times newspaper about wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but multiplication: BY.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark fruit of the elder tree is a classic base for country wines.

clue.text: Gorilla at bananas? It could be in zoo

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so these letters go wild into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A zoo-goer wonders whether the gorilla is eating bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the gorilla's food but means mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Large reptiles like this crocodilian are a familiar zoo exhibit, so it is defined by example of where one is found.

clue.text: Squeeze money out of some miserable editor

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone extorts cash from a wretched newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed someone is an idiom for draining them of money by repeated demands.

clue.text: Pick ridiculous expression about cold method of dispatch

parts.note: to pick is to elect or choose

indicators.note: about says the word for ridiculous goes around the cold letter

parts.note: rich in the sense of 'that's rich!', meaning absurd
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
an air is an expression or look on someone's face

explanation.surface: Choosing a silly phrase about a chilly way of getting rid of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' meaning ridiculous, as in 'that's a bit rich', is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: This device was a means of execution, and dispatch is a euphemism for killing.

clue.text: Order in vessels, small, very deep

indicators.note: in places the order's letters inside the vessels

parts.note: bottles are vessels
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Orders placed for containers, small, very deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour, abbreviated OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a floor seems infinitely deep, so the word is a hyperbole for very deep.

clue.text: Flood finished chap the Spanish abandoned

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: abandoned says these letters are dropped from the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A man who has given up on Spain is swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood is to spill over the brim, the same as this verb for liquid spilling out.

clue.text: Standard-bearer indicates runner in Cardiff

parts.note: to flag something up is to point it out
the Taff is the river that runs through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A sports report pointing to an athlete competing in the Welsh capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is a river, the Taff in Cardiff, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole that holds up a flag literally bears a standard, which is another word for a flag.

clue.text: Stick ambassador in the middle

indicators.note: in says the ambassador's letters sit inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the core is the middle of something
HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy is stuck in the centre of something.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the form of address for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together is to bond or hold fast, which is what particles or arguments do when they hang together.

clue.text: Heath upended board to go ashore

indicators.note: upended in a down clue says the word for board is read bottom to top

parts.note: room and board, lodging
to land is to go ashore

explanation.surface: A passenger turns over a plank before disembarking on the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: Board means lodging, as in room and board.
explanation.definitionFit: A heath is open uncultivated upland, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: What, in time, controlled capital

indicators.note: in places the query word inside the letters for time and controlled

parts.note: to have run a business is to have controlled it
eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what was in charge in a given period.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Iran.

clue.text: Emperor beginning to hate English pope

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Adrian IV, Nicholas Breakspear, was the only English pope

explanation.surface: An emperor starts to loathe the English pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Roman emperor who built the wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Give up gold points in panic

indicators.note: in places the gold and points letters inside the word for panic

parts.note: panic is fear
or is the heraldic word for gold
S and W are compass points, south and west

explanation.surface: A panicky trader abandons gold when prices tip.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry, and compass points give single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce something under oath is to give it up formally.

clue.text: Record one volume, for example

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
a tome is a book or volume

explanation.surface: A record, a single volume, given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a perfect model or typical instance of something.

clue.text: A course of action ending in surly indifference

parts.note: a path is a course you take

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A way of behaving that ends in sullen not caring.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is lack of interest or concern, plain indifference.

clue.text: Service chiefs (American) work with ruler and current procedure

parts.note: MoD is the Ministry of Defence, the head office of the British armed services
US for United States, so American
op is short for opus, a musical work
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Military top brass, an American, and royal involvement in some procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence; ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means a way of working, a standard method or procedure.

clue.text: Rocket launchers initially led by the nose

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, launches rockets

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Space engineers are led around by the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal sound is produced through the nose, so the adjective describes speech coming by that route.

clue.text: Horse mushrooms, more than enough for birds

indicators.note: the letters sit inside a phrase longer than the answer, so the phrase holds more than is needed

explanation.surface: A huge crop of horse mushrooms, more than flightless birds can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: These large flightless Australian runners are birds.

clue.text: She would display initiative finally in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution says the letters are turned round and read backwards
display says the letters are on show within the word that follows
finally says the letters are taken from the end of that word

explanation.surface: Someone shows enterprise at last during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five letters of 'initiative', read backwards, give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's name, best known from the musical about Eva Perón, so a female figure answers to the pronoun.

clue.text: Change poles for stopping streetcar

indicators.note: stopping as in plugging a gap, so the vehicle's letters are filled with the others

parts.note: a streetcar is the American word for a tram
N and S are the north and south poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Electrical poles being changed halt the trams.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to change something completely.

clue.text: Last of experiments with canny bloodsucker

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: with means and, together
fly is slang for shrewd or canny

explanation.surface: The final experiment ends with a shrewd vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: This small biting insect feeds on blood, so it is literally a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Study large people's gravestones

parts.note: to do a subject is to study it
L is the size label for large
men's, belonging to people or men

explanation.surface: Research into the burial markers of large people.
explanation.definitionFit: These prehistoric stone tables were often tombs, so they are megalithic grave markers.
